With that half settled the remaining half is quorum reachability, so the harness gained a configuration-change probe: the same five-voter phantom history now attempts to remove either a phantom voter (leaving three consistent voters in the new quorum) or a consistent voter (leaving a new quorum that includes a phantom). interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the phantom log claim left by an accepted InstallSnapshot changes how a server decides votes, and the same starvation also blocks configuration changes whose new quorum would include such a server. Vote half, decided by the retained receipt (execution ca11633cbde949dba0da0b9950651148; setup at event index 0, probe at index 1): the shared prefix ends at 42, the deposed leader and one follower hold an uncommitted suffix to 82 in term 2, the majority leader's snapshot sits at 63 in term 3, and both minority members therefore cache a claim (82, term 2) above an installed snapshot (63, term 3) while a majority voter keeps a consistent claim (63, term 3). One RequestVote with term 4 and the candidate's real claim (82, term 2), carrying the leadership-transfer flag, was delivered to both: the phantom granted it (response term 4) and the consistent voter rejected it (response term 4, granted false), so the same request produced different decisions and the granted authority rested on entries the voter's own snapshot had superseded (candidate last log term 2 below snapshot term 3). Source basis for the difference: requestVote evaluates completeness with getLastEntry (src_request_vote, raft.go 1626-1758, test at 1725-1748), which prefers the cached claim whenever it is at or above the snapshot index (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174), and installSnapshot never resets that claim (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977). Reachability half: a phantom suffix lies beyond the commit index of its term, so its holders are a minority of that configuration, and the configuration steps that would make them a quorum are themselves blocked because a newly appended configuration commits under the new configuration's quorum (src_append_config, raft.go 1204-1243, which installs the new configuration into the commitment before the entry commits), and the phantom cannot acknowledge any AppendEntries because its cached claim fails every prev-log check (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606). Local construction runs of the new probe show the asymmetry: removing a phantom voter committed immediately under the same load, while removing a consistent voter did not commit within five seconds, which is the first step of any shrink toward a phantom-only voter set. Limits: the config-change probe has no retained receipt yet; the described wedge of subsequent configuration changes stays source-derived and unmeasured; the vote half is measured in one five-voter history with the transfer flag, and a plain campaign never reaches the log test because the known-leader rejection fires first; configuration changes that are attempted before the phantom state arises, repeated phantom generations and larger clusters are unmeasured.
counterevidence: The parent question's repair probe shows the phantom claim is a transient state within a term: a snapshot published above the claim restores consistency, so neither the vote effect nor the config-change effect persists once the leader's snapshot index passes the claim.

The blocked configuration change is also a protective interaction: the steps that would shrink the voter set down to the phantom group cannot commit, so the phantom grant cannot be converted into authority over committed entries through a configuration change in the measured history.

Both minority members hold the same phantom claim, so the candidate in the probe is a real node with a real log claim, not a synthetic one; the only supplied element is the leadership-transfer flag on its request.
limitations: The vote decision is measured in one history; the config-change outcome is currently construction feedback only and its receipt is requested with this update.

The blocked removal leaves the leader with a locally adopted latest configuration that has not committed, which per source would also close the leader's configuration-change gate; that second-order wedge is unmeasured.

scope.description: Two cases built on the already validated five-voter phantom history: forty entries committed on all voters, the current leader and one follower partitioned together and given forty further entries that never reach a quorum of five, the remaining three voters electing a leader, committing twenty entries and publishing a snapshot at an index below the suffix end so both minority members become phantom holders after healing. One case then removes a phantom voter; the other removes a consistent follower. Both removals are issued on the majority leader and awaited for five seconds, and the phantom premise is recorded before the attempt.

The comparison between the two cases holds the history, snapshot index, timing and leader load identical; only the identity of the removed voter differs, and it is chosen so the new configuration's quorum either excludes or includes a phantom holder.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.

experiment.prefix: Each case repeats the phantom setup: elect a leader in a five-voter cluster, commit forty entries, partition the leader with one follower, drive forty further applies on the deposed leader so the pair shares an uncommitted suffix, wait for the pair to stop leading, wait for one of the remaining three to be the only stable leader, commit twenty entries there and force Snapshot(), heal the partition and wait until both minority members have installed the snapshot. The case then records the premise (claim above snapshot on both minority members, consistent claim on a majority voter) and issues RemoveServer on the majority leader for either a phantom holder or a consistent follower, waiting up to five seconds for the future and recording whether it committed, the elapsed time, the configuration sizes the leader reports before and after, and whether the removed voter held a phantom claim.
semantic_changes: The phantom scenario gained an optional configuration-change attempt selecting the removed voter's role, with a five-second bounded wait and the leader's reported configuration sizes recorded before and after.

scope.description: Two real three-voter cluster histories in one process: a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is then restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. In the trimmed case the leader's log store is compacted to TrailingLogs=10 so it can only repair by shipping that snapshot; in the control TrailingLogs is large so entries alone can repair. Each case samples the victim's restores, applied index, commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range, plus the cluster frontier, for a 3s window with steady new writes.

excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.

scope.description: Two new cases of the same three-voter history, each built on the unchanged scenario (isolated leader appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot, isolated node restarted on its real log store and reconnected). Case two keeps the non-monotonic store and, once the stall is established, drives the leader's applied index past the follower's cached claim and publishes a snapshot above it, then keeps sampling to see whether the follower resumes accepting entries.

Case two adds only: entries applied on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, then one forced Snapshot(); the stall is measured before those additions.

basis.prefix: Same scenario driver as the earlier revisions, now parameterised by log-store monotonicity and by an optional repair step. Case one: the trimmed history runs with MonotonicLogs=true; the follower's install deletes its entire log store, and the probe reports whether installs repeat, whether the follower reaches the frontier, whether the cached claim persists, and whether any suffix above the snapshot index survived in the store. interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the phantom log claim produced by the InstallSnapshot path changes how a server decides votes, because requestVote evaluates log completeness with getLastEntry, which prefers the cached claim over the installed snapshot. Source basis: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); requestVote's completeness test rejects only when the voter's last term is greater than the candidate's, or equal with a greater index (src_vote_log_check, raft.go 1725-1748 inside requestVote at 1626-1758); installSnapshot never resets that cached entry (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977). Consequence: a voter whose snapshot already contains committed entries in a newer term will still grant a vote to a candidate whose last log entry carries an older term, whenever the cached claim wins the comparison - exactly the case a voter comparing against its snapshot would reject. The scope is bounded rather than established as a safety break: the phantom suffix was never committed (a quorum storing it would have committed it), so its holders were a minority of the configuration that created it, and a leader's snapshot index cannot fall below committed history; a quorum of phantom voters therefore needs a configuration change that turns that minority into a majority of a new configuration. The affected direction is also milder than the phrasing 'stale rejection' suggests: the claim can both reject candidates whose last term equals the claimed term with a lower index and grant candidates whose last term is below the snapshot's term. Limits: this account is source-derived plus local construction feedback (the five-voter probe behaved as predicted: phantom granted, consistent voter rejected, candidate term below the phantom's snapshot term); it has no retained receipt yet, the vote effect is unmeasured in 3-voter configurations, and the configuration-change path that could turn phantom holders into a quorum is not measured at all.
counterevidence: The same root cause in the progress direction was measured to be bounded: starvation ends once a snapshot above the cached claim is published (parent question receipt), so the phantom claim is a transient state within a term, not a permanent log corruption.

A phantom suffix lies beyond the commit index of the term that created it, so its holders are a minority of that configuration; the parent account already argues that a quorum of phantoms then needs a configuration change, which no measurement here supports.

result.summary: Interpreted the child receipt (ca11633cbde949dba0da0b9950651148, exit 0, test passed): all four vote comparisons are complete and hold — one identical RequestVote (term 4, candidate claim (82, term 2), leadership-transfer flag) was granted by the phantom holder (claim (82, term 2) over its installed snapshot at 63/term 3) and rejected by the majority voter whose claim matched its snapshot (63, term 3), so the same request produced different decisions and the granted authority rested on entries the voter's own snapshot superseded. scope.description: Two real three-voter cluster histories in one process: a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is then restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. In the trimmed case the leader's log store is compacted to TrailingLogs=10 so it can only repair by shipping that snapshot; in the control TrailingLogs is large so entries alone can repair. Each case samples the victim's restores, applied index, commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range, plus the cluster frontier, for a 3s window with steady new writes.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced event is a full transport partition of one voter plus its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.

excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.

Basis, source side: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail), getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry), the non-monotonic compaction path cannot remove a suffix that still lies above the snapshot index (src_compaction), every prev-log check then misses or mismatches so the leader only decrements nextIndex one step at a time (src_replicate_failure) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the newest snapshot, after which nextIndex is reset to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result).
